questions.title: The monomer and linkage of amylose
questions.question: The structural monosaccharides residues that make up the amylose chain are exactly which of the following?

options.A: The entirely repeating simple fructose units in alpha linkages
options.B: The completely identical single galactose units in alpha linkages
options.D: The entirely repeating simple mannose units in alpha linkages

explanations.A: Incorrect. Fructose is not amylose's building block; amylose is built entirely of glucose.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Galactose is not amylose's building block either — it is a component of lactose and some glycolipids, not of starch.
explanations.C: Correct. Amylose is the linear, unbranched part of starch, built from D-glucose units joined by alpha-1,4-glucosidic bonds with no branching. This is the same backbone linkage amylopectin uses, but amylose lacks amylopectin's added alpha-1,6 branch points. Glucose in alpha linkages is therefore the correct description of amylose's residues.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Mannose is not amylose's building block; it appears in other glycoconjugates, not in starch.

questions.learning_objective: State that amylose is built of glucose joined by alpha-1,4 linkages, with no branching.
